evidence_labels.VERIFIED: Confirmed from an identified source page, metadata record or exact dataset documentation.
evidence_labels.MEASURED: The exact source was downloaded or queried and joined to the stable 91-country universe.
evidence_labels.ESTIMATED: Phase 3C analyst judgement; not a completed coverage or licensing audit.

phase3e_shortlist.name: Existing immigrant share
phase3e_shortlist.rationale: Proceed to deterministic Phase 3E probe; measured current coverage is 91/91.

phase3e_shortlist.name: Overall job-market opportunity
phase3e_shortlist.rationale: Proceed to a deterministic Phase 3E probe. The measured 88/91 intersection clears the 82-country threshold but requires an explicit missing-country policy.

phase3e_shortlist.name: School education quality
phase3e_shortlist.rationale: Proceed to deterministic Phase 3E probe; measured field coverage is 89/91 and the source is current, official and reusable.

records.name: Overall job-market opportunity
records.description: A narrow national composite of modelled unemployment, employment-to-population ratio and labour-force participation for total population age 15+.
records.relocation_question: How strong is the destination's national labour market for a working-age newcomer, before occupation-specific matching?
records.definition: A narrow national composite of modelled unemployment, employment-to-population ratio and labour-force participation for total population age 15+.

scoring.proposed_method: Reverse unemployment; robust-percentile each component; average only after correlation and weight sensitivity checks.

comparability_notes: [VERIFIED] ILO modelled estimates use a common statistical system and identical age/sex dimensions.
[ESTIMATED] The three components partly duplicate one latent labour-utilisation factor.
country_mapping_notes: [MEASURED] ISO3 joined deterministically; ATG, GRD and UKR were absent from all three 2025 slices.
licensing_notes: [VERIFIED] ILO datasets and referential metadata published from 3 May 2023 are CC BY 4.0; restricted partner microdata are excluded.
maintenance_notes: Annual edition pinning is required; projections beyond the edition's current year must not be mixed with observed/modelled current-year values.
records.recommendation: Proceed to a deterministic Phase 3E probe. The measured 88/91 intersection clears the 82-country threshold but requires an explicit missing-country policy.
open_questions: Should C11 remain a composite or expose unemployment and employment separately?
Is 2025 accepted as a modelled current-year value?

evidence.claim: The three exact ILOSTAT 2025 total/15+ series each returned 88 stable countries; common missing ISO3 codes were ATG, GRD and UKR.
The ILOSTAT catalogue labels the series as Nov. 2025 modelled estimates and exposes reproducible bulk CSV downloads.
ILOSTAT data licence is CC BY 4.0 for datasets published from 3 May 2023.

records.name: Skilled-work visa accessibility
records.description: A profile-derived eligibility and friction assessment, not a destination-only national score.
records.relocation_question: Given a person's nationality, occupation, qualifications, salary and employer situation, how feasible is a lawful skilled-work route?
records.definition: A profile-derived eligibility and friction assessment, not a destination-only national score.

scoring.proposed_method: Rule-engine eligibility plus route-specific friction; no standalone country percentile.

comparability_notes: [VERIFIED] EU rules depend on job offer, salary threshold, qualifications and member-state implementation.
[ESTIMATED] OECD ITA is useful discovery evidence but OECD-only and broader than visa accessibility.
country_mapping_notes: Country is insufficient: origin, profession, employer, salary and family status alter eligibility.
licensing_notes: OECD default open-access policy is not a substitute for checking the exact 2023 tool export; EC-owned portal content is CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise indicated.
maintenance_notes: Legal rules and thresholds require frequent country-by-country change detection and dated snapshots.
records.recommendation: Defer to a future profile/legal-mobility layer. Reject it as an independent destination criterion.
open_questions: Which origin passports and occupations define the first supported profiles?

evidence.claim: The EU portal applies to 25 EU countries and describes job-offer, qualification and salary conditions.
OECD ITA 2023 compares talent attractiveness for highly educated workers but is limited to OECD countries.
No current official global dataset was verified that converts individual skilled-work eligibility into comparable destination scores.

records.name: Permanent-residency accessibility
records.description: A route-specific legal pathway assessment covering qualifying residence, permit continuity, income/language conditions and exclusions.
records.relocation_question: For a specific migrant route and personal history, what lawful path exists to permanent residence and on what conditions?
records.definition: A route-specific legal pathway assessment covering qualifying residence, permit continuity, income/language conditions and exclusions.

scoring.proposed_method: Eligibility timeline and conditions by route; informational result rather than a destination-only score.

comparability_notes: SDG 10.7.2 measures broad well-managed migration policy, not personal permanent-residence eligibility.
National terminology and qualifying residence rules are not harmonised.
country_mapping_notes: Route and legal-history mapping dominate ISO country mapping.
licensing_notes: UN website terms permit personal non-commercial use and prohibit redistribution/derivatives absent a specific licence.
maintenance_notes: Requires dated legal rules, legal-review governance and frequent change detection.
records.recommendation: Defer to a route-aware profile layer; reject a single national accessibility score.
open_questions: Whether permanent residence and citizenship pathways should be separate product modules.

evidence.claim: The current official SDG 10.7.2 update is based on 2018–2021 government inquiries and measures broad migration-policy domains.
Generic UN website terms do not provide production-compatible reuse for a derived commercial dataset.
No authoritative, current, global route-level permanent-residence dataset was verified.

records.name: Average earning potential
records.description: Average monthly employee earnings converted to PPP, with explicit limits as a national proxy for personal earning potential.
records.relocation_question: What gross earning level could a typical employee plausibly attain, before occupation and city adjustments?
records.definition: Average monthly employee earnings converted to PPP, with explicit limits as a national proxy for personal earning potential.

scoring.proposed_method: Log PPP earnings, winsorise tails, then robust percentile; do not treat as expected salary for a user.

comparability_notes: Employee coverage, informal work, hours and source instruments vary.
PPP improves price comparability but does not remove occupation or city composition effects.
country_mapping_notes: ISO3 is stable; the substantive blocker is observation availability.
licensing_notes: ILOSTAT dataset and metadata are CC BY 4.0.
maintenance_notes: Currency and PPP classifications must be pinned; source breaks and multiple national observations need deterministic precedence.
records.recommendation: Defer. Measured recent PPP earnings coverage is 60/91 for 2023+ and 76/91 for 2021+, below the Phase 3A threshold.
open_questions: Whether a different official income concept can recover 82+ countries without changing the question.

evidence.claim: EAR_EMTA_SEX_CUR_NB_A PPP observations covered 76 stable countries from 2021 onward and 60 from 2023 onward.
The exact ILOSTAT table was updated 19 July 2026 and spans through 2026.

records.name: Personal income-tax burden
records.description: A household-scenario tax wedge or net personal average tax rate, not a universal national rate.
records.relocation_question: For a given salary, household and employment arrangement, what share of labour cost or gross earnings is taken by income tax and mandatory contributions?
records.definition: A household-scenario tax wedge or net personal average tax rate, not a universal national rate.

scoring.proposed_method: Compute net burden for explicit salary and household scenarios; lower is not automatically better without service-benefit context.

comparability_notes: OECD methodology is highly comparable inside 38 OECD members but not globally representative.
Results change by earnings level, household type and social-contribution treatment.
country_mapping_notes: Country mapping is straightforward; tax-unit and household mapping are not.
licensing_notes: OECD content from July 2024 is generally CC BY 4.0, subject to exact-page exceptions and third-party material.
maintenance_notes: Annual tax-law parameter updates and scenario versioning are required.
records.recommendation: Defer to a profile-based affordability calculator; do not use the OECD-only series as a 91-country ranking criterion.
open_questions: Which standard household and salary scenarios would be product-supported?

evidence.claim: Taxing Wages 2026 covers the 38 OECD countries and reports 2025 tax wedges/net personal average rates by household type.
The exact comparative Data Explorer family is DSD_TAX_WAGES_COMP@DF_TW_COMP.

records.name: Housing affordability
records.description: City-level rent or ownership cost divided by profile-specific disposable income, with tenure and household size explicit.
records.relocation_question: Can the user's household afford suitable housing in the destination city on its expected disposable income?
records.definition: City-level rent or ownership cost divided by profile-specific disposable income, with tenure and household size explicit.

scoring.proposed_method: Profile-specific housing-cost share; national price-to-income only as context.

comparability_notes: HC1.2 total housing costs are available mainly for European countries plus New Zealand and definitions differ.
National ratios conceal metropolitan rent dispersion.
country_mapping_notes: Requires city/metro identifiers, tenure, bedrooms and household composition.
licensing_notes: OECD open-access policy is favourable; exact workbook/front-page licence still needs capture in implementation.
maintenance_notes: Fast-moving city rents and disposable incomes require more frequent updates than annual national statistics.
records.recommendation: Defer to the city and profile layers. National OECD ratios are useful validation data, not the independent criterion.
open_questions: City universe, rental unit specification and household scenarios.

evidence.claim: OECD HC1.2 is an exact housing-cost-over-income table, but its documentation says total housing costs are available only for European countries and New Zealand.
The Affordable Housing Database is explicitly OECD/EU/key-partner focused.

records.name: Healthcare system capacity and quality
records.description: UHC service coverage index as a national capacity/access proxy; it does not directly measure migrant entitlement, waiting times or care experience.
records.relocation_question: How capable is the national health system of delivering broad essential care, acknowledging that migrant eligibility may differ?
records.definition: UHC service coverage index as a national capacity/access proxy; it does not directly measure migrant entitlement, waiting times or care experience.

scoring.proposed_method: Use the published 0–100 index directly after freshness and licence gates.

comparability_notes: The index is a geometric mean of 14 tracers; not every tracer directly measures service coverage.
National population coverage does not establish migrant entitlement or local access.
country_mapping_notes: World Bank representation maps cleanly to ISO3.
licensing_notes: World Bank representation is CC BY 4.0; direct WHO commercial reuse requires permission or a dataset-specific compatible licence.
maintenance_notes: Monitor for the 2023 WHO revision to enter a production-compatible World Bank distribution and for methodology breaks.
records.recommendation: Defer now. The reusable World Bank representation is complete but remains at 2021; the fresh 2023 WHO release has unresolved commercial reuse for direct ingestion.
open_questions: When will the World Bank CC BY representation refresh to the revised 2023 series?

evidence.claim: The current World Bank HNP API returned 91/91 stable countries, all with latest year 2021.
The 2025 global monitoring release reports the UHC service coverage index through 2023.
WHO requires permission for commercial use of WHO materials absent a more specific licence.

records.name: English usability
records.description: A local usability concept combining institutional language availability and population proficiency; national adult test scores are only a weak proxy.
records.relocation_question: How easily can an English-speaking newcomer handle work, services and daily life in the specific destination?
records.definition: A local usability concept combining institutional language availability and population proficiency; national adult test scores are only a weak proxy.

scoring.proposed_method: No independent score until native-English destinations and institutional usability have equivalent measures.

comparability_notes: EF test takers are self-selected, young-skewed and internet-only.
Adult proficiency is not the same as service or workplace usability; native-English destinations are not symmetrically observed.
country_mapping_notes: EF includes countries/regions and thresholded cities; stable-country and native-language exceptions require policy.
licensing_notes: Raw data are not prepared for external sharing; no dataset-specific production licence was verified.
maintenance_notes: Annual edition changes and city sample thresholds create unstable coverage.
records.recommendation: Defer to a city/preference layer. Do not use EF EPI as a production country criterion.
open_questions: Whether English usability should be a user preference/filter rather than a ranked criterion.

evidence.claim: EF EPI 2025 uses more than 2.2 million 2024 test takers, but the sample is self-selected and not guaranteed representative.
EF states that its raw source data are not prepared for sharing outside the organisation.

records.name: Overall higher-education opportunity
records.description: Gross tertiary enrolment ratio as a national participation proxy; it is not a university-quality or migrant-access measure.
records.relocation_question: How broad is access to tertiary education in the destination, before institution, field, tuition and international-student constraints?
records.definition: Gross tertiary enrolment ratio as a national participation proxy; it is not a university-quality or migrant-access measure.

scoring.proposed_method: Robust percentile only as tertiary participation; do not label it quality or international-student opportunity.

comparability_notes: Gross enrolment can exceed 100 and reflects system participation, not teaching quality, places for foreigners, tuition or field availability.
country_mapping_notes: ISO3 mapping is clean; small states have sparse updates.
licensing_notes: World Bank representation is CC BY 4.0; direct UIS browser data are CC BY-SA 4.0.
maintenance_notes: Annual UIS/WDI release; pin extraction date and latest-observation rule.
records.recommendation: Experimental/recovery probe only. Overall coverage is 88/91, but only 77/91 have 2023+ data and 81/91 have 2021+ data.
open_questions: Can a second UIS participation/completion series recover at least 82 fresh countries without changing semantics?

evidence.claim: The WDI API returned 88/91 with any 2010–2025 value, 81/91 at 2021+, and 77/91 at 2023+.
WDI metadata identifies UIS as upstream, annual periodicity and CC BY 4.0.

records.name: Existing immigrant share
records.description: International migrant stock as a percentage of total population, using UN Population Division estimates distributed by WDI.
records.relocation_question: How established is international migration in the destination, as indicated by the foreign-born share of residents?
records.definition: International migrant stock as a percentage of total population, using UN Population Division estimates distributed by WDI.

scoring.proposed_method: Logit-transform percentage, winsorise, then robust percentile; keep interpretation as established migrant presence, not friendliness.

comparability_notes: Foreign-born is used where possible; citizenship is substituted in some countries and missing countries are imputed.
Stock reflects history and geography, not current visa openness or lived inclusion.
country_mapping_notes: WDI ISO3 mapping is deterministic; country breakups create historical discontinuities.
licensing_notes: The exact WDI representation is CC BY 4.0, avoiding restrictive generic UN website terms.
maintenance_notes: Slow-moving; pin UN revision and WDI release.
records.recommendation: Proceed to deterministic Phase 3E probe; measured current coverage is 91/91.
open_questions: Whether scoring should be higher-better or informational/preference based.

evidence.claim: The WDI API returned 2024 observations for all 91 stable countries.
WDI metadata identifies UN Population Division as publisher, describes census/register/survey inputs and imputation, and assigns CC BY 4.0.

records.name: Software and technology jobs
records.description: Employment in selected ISCO-08 two-digit ICT-related occupations as a national proxy; vacancies and city concentration remain unmeasured.
records.relocation_question: How large and accessible is the software/technology employment market in the relevant city for the user's occupation?
records.definition: Employment in selected ISCO-08 two-digit ICT-related occupations as a national proxy; vacancies and city concentration remain unmeasured.

scoring.proposed_method: Selected ICT occupation employment divided by total employment; experimental only after occupation-code review.

comparability_notes: Two-digit occupation groups are broader than software jobs and miss tech-industry roles outside selected occupations.
National employment stocks do not measure vacancies, hiring friction or city clusters.
country_mapping_notes: ISO3 is deterministic; ISCO version and occupation-code mapping require version controls.
maintenance_notes: ISCO revisions, survey breaks and city labour-market sourcing would be substantial.
records.recommendation: Defer to a city/occupation layer. Recent two-digit occupation data cover only 66/91 and remain semantically too broad.
open_questions: Whether to define tech by occupation, industry, vacancies, or a hybrid.

evidence.claim: EMP_TEMP_SEX_OC2_NB_A had 2023+ observations for 66/91 stable countries.
ILOSTAT exposes occupation data only up to ISCO two-digit level in the relevant public table family.

records.name: Internet access, speed, and reliability
records.description: Current reusable sources support national internet use and fixed-broadband penetration, not a complete speed/reliability measure.
records.relocation_question: Can a newcomer expect affordable, fast and dependable connectivity where they live and work?
records.definition: Current reusable sources support national internet use and fixed-broadband penetration, not a complete speed/reliability measure.

scoring.proposed_method: Experimental access/penetration composite only; do not label it speed and reliability.

comparability_notes: Internet use and fixed-broadband subscriptions are comparable but are not throughput, latency, outages or affordability.
country_mapping_notes: WDI ISO3 mapping is already validated in the repository.
licensing_notes: WDI representations are CC BY 4.0; direct ITU DataHub is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO and unsuitable for commercial production.
maintenance_notes: Annual WDI refresh is manageable; a true speed/reliability source would require faster updates and city/geospatial policy.
records.recommendation: Experimental/redundancy probe only for a narrowed access-and-penetration criterion. Do not claim speed or reliability.
open_questions: Whether this adds value beyond the existing infrastructure experiment and whether speed should be city-level.

evidence.claim: The repository's existing source audit measured both WDI components at 91/91; latest internet-use observations were 2024–25 and fixed broadband 2023–24.
ITU DataHub describes about 200 economies and direct data under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO.

records.name: Electricity access and reliability
records.description: Electricity-access percentage plus an outage/reliability outcome; only access currently meets global coverage.
records.relocation_question: Can a household and workplace expect continuous electricity service, not merely a grid connection?
records.definition: Electricity-access percentage plus an outage/reliability outcome; only access currently meets global coverage.

scoring.proposed_method: Access higher-better and outages lower-better; no combined score until reliability clears coverage.

comparability_notes: Access is near-ceiling in much of the stable universe and is not reliability.
Enterprise Survey outages reflect sampled firms, subnational survey locations and heterogeneous survey years.
country_mapping_notes: ISO3 is straightforward; subnational survey strata do not map to a national lived-experience claim.
licensing_notes: World Bank series are CC BY 4.0.
maintenance_notes: Reliability requires survey-year and coverage controls; access alone adds little differentiation.
records.recommendation: Defer. Access measured 91/91 for 2024, but the WDI API returned no observations for IC.ELC.OUTG; access alone does not answer reliability.
open_questions: A global reusable SAIDI/SAIFI or household-outage source with 82+ stable-country coverage.

evidence.claim: EG.ELC.ACCS.ZS returned 2024 observations for all 91 stable countries.
The current WDI API query for IC.ELC.OUTG returned zero stable-country observations.

records.name: School education quality
records.description: HCI+ harmonized learning outcomes and learning-adjusted years of schooling, used as national outcome measures.
records.relocation_question: How much effective learning does the national school system produce for a child, before local school choice?
records.definition: HCI+ harmonized learning outcomes and learning-adjusted years of schooling, used as national outcome measures.

scoring.proposed_method: Prefer the published schooling component or learning-adjusted years; test sensitivity against HLO alone.

comparability_notes: Harmonized learning outcomes bridge different assessments through a common scale and modelling.
National averages mask region, school sector, language and migrant-child access.
country_mapping_notes: ISO3 mapping was deterministic; BHS and BOL lacked the tested schooling/learning fields.
maintenance_notes: Pin HCI+ version and clarify whether file year 2025 is an estimate; catalogue temporal metadata says 2009–2024 while the file contains 2025 labels.
records.recommendation: Proceed to deterministic Phase 3E probe; measured field coverage is 89/91 and the source is current, official and reusable.
open_questions: Use the schooling component, LAYS, or HLO as the primary score?

evidence.claim: The downloaded HCI+ panel contained 89/91 stable countries for HLO/LAYS; BHS and BOL were missing. Eighty-eight had latest labels at 2024+ for HLO/LAYS.
The catalogue states 166-country coverage, national granularity, file update 11 February 2026 and CC BY 4.0.

records.name: Extreme-weather risk
records.description: A transparent subset of INFORM 2026 hazard scores: river flood, tropical cyclone, coastal flood and drought; earthquakes, tsunamis, epidemics and conflict are excluded.
records.relocation_question: How exposed is the destination to severe weather-related hazards that could disrupt life, property and services?
records.definition: A transparent subset of INFORM 2026 hazard scores: river flood, tropical cyclone, coastal flood and drought; earthquakes, tsunamis, epidemics and conflict are excluded.

source_candidates.series_or_table: INFORM_Risk_2026_v072.xlsx: River Flood, Tropical Cyclone, Coastal flood, Drought

scoring.proposed_method: Experimental maximum or weighted mean of the four published 0–10 hazards; publish sensitivity and avoid calling it the official INFORM Natural score.

comparability_notes: The official Natural score also includes geophysical and epidemic hazards, so it is semantically too broad.
The selected subset omits heatwaves, wildfire, severe convective storms and local adaptation.
country_mapping_notes: All 91 stable ISO3 codes mapped and had values in each selected field.
licensing_notes: INFORM calls results open; EC-owned site content defaults to CC BY 4.0, but workbook source-data chains require a dataset-specific third-party-rights check before production.
maintenance_notes: Pin workbook version and component names; monitor annual methodology changes.
records.recommendation: Experimental Phase 3E probe only. Coverage is complete, but a Konsider-specific weather subset and weighting need defensibility testing.
open_questions: Whether heatwave and wildfire omissions are acceptable
Confirm workbook-level reuse and upstream source chain.

evidence.claim: The downloaded INFORM Risk 2026 v072 workbook mapped all 91 stable ISO3 codes and had non-null River Flood, Tropical Cyclone, Coastal flood and Drought scores for every country.
INFORM describes the index as global and open and publishes the workbook with source data and calculation steps.
EC-owned website content is CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise indicated, with third-party-rights caveats.
